# Three things

Here's what caught my attention this week:

### [Can You Afford to Watch TV?](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/02/arts/television/streaming-tv-era-cost.html) (article)

This piece provides some viewpoints on the impact subscriptions have on audience's ability to watch television.
The author uses the analogy that TV consumption is like "high-end dining."
Indeed, a point is made in the piece that such an environment hurts the medium and creates divisions in experiences for audiences.
I found this quote from the article worth some additional reflection:

> The stories you experience and the references you get are determined by the purchase decisions you've made.

### [Does AI drive more direct traffic?](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/does-ai-drive-more-direct-traffic) (blog)

This post explores and discusses the AI traffic that might be hidden in Direct web traffic.
The author cites an [interview](https://www.siegemedia.com/conversation/how-ramp-accurately-tracks-ai-traffic-w-eric-wiu) that states 30 to 40% of direct traffic is originating from answer engines.
However, this post's analysis couldn't find any hidden AI traffic within their Direct traffic when exploring a sample of B2B and B2C websites.
The post did find a correlation between AI visibility and Direct after a three-week delay. Though when it was parsed further, the relationship didn't hold.
To summarize, the author suggests a rethinking of the traditional click funnel (i.e., search -> click -> convert).

### [Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?](https://www.theverge.com/podcast/1000344/cloudflare-matthew-prince-google-zero-ai-web-advertising) (podcast)

Recently, I've been on a [Decoder podcast](https://www.theverge.com/decoder-podcast-with-nilay-patel) kick, catching up on episodes I've missed.
Here's another interesting interview with [Cloudflare's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloudflare) CEO, [Matthew Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Prince).
If you're a part of the media industry, you'll want to listen from [04M51S to 46M37S](https://youtu.be/4t8RhKbkb70?si=dsmstfai362TlhdO&t=291).
Here are some specific points in the interview that I tagged as interesting:

* [04M17S](https://youtu.be/4t8RhKbkb70?si=dsmstfai362TlhdO&t=291): The business model of the internet, and is it still working?
* [14M20S](https://youtu.be/4t8RhKbkb70?si=zLAuunzKUVIi_z2m&t=860): Tragedy of the commons. Every request on the internet has an associated cost, whether it's a human or an agent.
* [24M00S](https://youtu.be/4t8RhKbkb70?si=C0wzd813cdhpWz1t&t=1440): The value of local news to LLMs.
* [37M00S](https://youtu.be/4t8RhKbkb70?si=HgfhCeaRTdWXX99g&t=2220): Information market driven by feeding valuable information to bots, is this a good thing?

Check out the links above for the full story in each item, not just my brief summary and analysis.

# What I found interesting this week

This week, I've been really focused on creating interactive tables for some data projects I'm working on.
The [DT](https://rstudio.github.io/DT/) package has always been my go to, which provides a straightforward interface to JavaScript's DataTables JavaScript library. 
However, I needed some functionality that I couldn't figure out how to do for one of my projects.
So, I went looking.

I came across the [reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/) R package.
Not only did I find what I was looking for, but I was excited to see all the package made available in terms of interactive tables.
I found the package's [Examples](https://glin.github.io/reactable/articles/examples.html) page to be a great place to see what was all available.
The interface was very similar in terms of DT, so before long I was getting the hang of it.
It made it easy to start.
